Markets Rally as Tech Earnings Beat Expectations

U.S. stocks climbed on Friday after several large technology companies reported quarterly earnings that exceeded Wall Street forecasts, lifting investor confidence in the sector's growth trajectory despite elevated interest rates.

Analysts said revenue guidance and margin expansion were the primary drivers behind the move, with fund managers rotating back into megacap names that had lagged earlier in the quarter. Trading volume rose across major indexes as options activity picked up ahead of the weekend.

Bond yields drifted lower as traders priced in a more gradual path for monetary policy, while currency markets remained subdued. Commodity prices were mixed, with industrial metals gaining on China stimulus hopes and energy slipping on inventory builds.

Portfolio managers noted that valuation multiples remain stretched in pockets of the market, but cash flows from leading software and semiconductor firms continue to support premium pricing. Several strategists raised year-end index targets citing resilient consumer spending and stabilizing input costs for manufacturers.

Looking ahead, investors will focus on next week's inflation report and a slate of retail earnings that could clarify whether demand is broadening beyond technology leaders. Risk assets may remain volatile if data surprise to the upside and revive rate-hike fears.
